title: a clean that fails partway leaves fullcycle reporting nothing about the links it darkened
body:
Found by critic-shell reviewing the fix for issue `0068` on 2026-09-16, by reading the code. Not reproduced in a run.

`lib/cmd/fullcycle` sets `cleaned=1` only when `clean rust` exits 0. `lib/cmd/clean` removes trees one at a time -- `rm -rf "$d" || die "could not remove $d"` inside a loop -- so a clean that fails can already have removed earlier trees, and `rm -rf` itself can fail partway through one.

With `cleaned` unset, both reports that exist for this damage are skipped: the loop's `THE BUILD TREES WERE ALREADY REMOVED` branch, and the after-half link check, which is gated on `cleaned`. A PATH link darkened by a partial clean is not reported. The run does go red, with `STOPPING: clean rust failed`, which reads as nothing having been touched.

## Why it is worth an issue

The link check needs no `cleaned` flag to be right: a link that resolved at the start and does not resolve now is evidence on its own. Gating it on a clean's exit code makes it blind in the one case where the clean's own report cannot be trusted either.

## Shape of a fix, not a ruling

Run the after-half link check whenever `atrisk` is non-empty, whatever the phases did. Say on a failed clean that it may have removed some trees before failing. Hold it with an arm: a clean stub that removes one tree and exits non-zero, with a watched link into the removed tree.
